sources: dossier=Required behaviors/Naming bullet (2026-05-12/13, artifact) establishes the Database→Tables()→per-row-type accessor vocabulary as the ground truth for what ledgers exist; doc=line 15 listed "schedules" as a persisted ledger; code=persistence.Tables interface has no Schedules accessor and neither postgres nor sqlite migrations define a rimsky_schedules table (grep across both migration trees returns no hits).
note: No dossier entry claims cron scheduling is persisted as its own ledger, and both backends' schema plus the Tables interface confirm no such ledger exists; removed "schedules" from the line-15 enumeration.

sources: dossier=Naming bullet (2026-05-12/13, artifact) plus the Node-run model bullet (2026-06-20, transcript) establish rimsky_node_runs as the real ledger; doc=line 15 said "node-events" while line 21 of the same doc already said "node-run ledgers", an internal contradiction; code=no NodeEvents accessor exists in persistence.Tables and no rimsky_node_events table exists in either backend's migrations; rimsky_node_runs is the real table (NodeRunTree() accessor, node_runs.go).
note: "node-events" was a phantom ledger name that also contradicted line 21 of the same doc; replaced with "node-runs", the real ledger the dossier's node-run model bullet and the Tables interface both confirm.

sources: dossier=Naming bullet establishes Tables() as the accessor umbrella but does not mandate an exhaustive prose enumeration; doc=line 15's parenthetical was phrased as a complete list yet omitted Messages, MessageIdempotencies, Lineage, PublisherSubscriptions, NodeRunTree, RunScopes, APIKeys, Breakpoints/BreakpointHits, and WaitSet, while line 13's analogous parenthetical already used "etc." to signal illustrative status; code=persistence.Tables lists all of these accessors.
note: Adopted the finding's first suggested remedy: marked the line-15 enumeration illustrative with a trailing "etc.", matching the pattern line 13 already uses for the umbrella bundle, rather than hand-maintaining an exhaustive list that will drift again as Tables() grows.

sources: dossier="One persistence driver per process is a blessed invariant" (2026-06-14, f0176bde, transcript) plus the memory-blob-backend gate tied to RIMSKY_PROCESS_ROLE=unified; doc=line 11 said "the three runtime processes hold it", implying three always-separate Database instances; code=StartUnifiedStack in the launch package takes a single injected persistence.Database and passes it to all three role runners (scheduler, supervisor, control-api) in the unified single-process deployment, and the doc's own invariant at line 34 (memory blob backend gated to the unified role) depends on that single shared instance.
note: The prior phrasing missed the unified single-process deployment, where one process runs all three roles and holds one shared database instance -- exactly the case the doc's own memory-blob invariant depends on. Reworded to distinguish the split deployment (three processes, three instances) from the unified deployment (one process, one shared instance).
